utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom. The witness should be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please sit down. May I remind you the affirmation, the solemn declaration, you made yesterday still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey has some more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ruez. We should have 178 up on the screen. I don't know if it's on your screen yet. It's -- and you had just described this orange water as the normal colour of this dam but you hadn't gotten, I don't believe, any further. You've got some blue arrows on this. What do those depict?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These arrows depict the way the two survivors of the execution that occurred on the dam -- depict the escape routes that UN later can match with their testimony, so first crawling into this ditch, then hitting the little wood which is on top of an elevation just in front, and then during the day of the 15th, they were crawling in order to hit a hill which is at the east of the dam. East on this picture, being at the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next -- your next photograph, 181. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, 179.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's the same indication, but one cannot see any longer the little wood, but the blue line going to the left represents roughly the way they took, and then they continued on the line on top of this hill until they could find their way, orienting themselves from the direction of Zvornik, and then trying to go across the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 180. We are now back to the water area. What -- why have you put this photograph in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, this one could have been erased from this presentation. This one was used at a time of another trial in order to explain the reason why some searchs, forensic searches that were done on this peninsula were unsuccessful, because it was a dump of chemicals and the forensic team had no means to continue to dig in such a chemical environment. But we will never know what is there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you have some reason or any information from the investigation that there may be bodies or evidence in that area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could be, because during the day of the 15, the two survivors could see that the loading of bodies that were scattering the ground on the plateau of the dam were taken by a little wheeled platform tracked by a tractor that could -- that took the direction that goes, in fact, up to the little dirt road that hits the peninsula. They couldn't see where this little tractor was going, but the assumption therefore was that the initial burial place that had been selected was not on the dam, but elsewhere. So whatever the amount of bodies we would have found in a grave on that location would not account for the total of number killed. Therefore, we were looking for the very first burial spot used by the Bosnian Serb army in this location. But again, because of this circumstances, this very first burial place was not found, but what we know anyhow is that on the 15 and excavator came and opened a hole on the plateau of this dam and buried the people who were still on the plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 181. And do you remember who this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for sure. That was the first time we arrived on this dam. So we did a very short collection on the surface, and among the items which we could gather were all these bones. And the person photographing the bones is Professor Bill Haglund, Richard Haglund -- William Haglund, sorry. And he is the anthropologist who assessed what these bones were, so human bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you say your first short visit, can you explain very briefly why you didn't stay longer? Why it was a short visit?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the missions during 1996 were very short because the goal was to go as soon as possible to locations that were already identified between August 1995 and March 1996, and the goal was to hit as many of them in a short period of time in order to have a first assessment of these places without necessarily conducting a thorough search on all of them. As everyone knows, time runs against evidence. And already a winter had passed. We already had the, in bracket, "luck" to assess these crime scenes in such a time-frame, because the war was over. And the goal was just to make sure that we were on the right place and then decide if we had to spark additional forensics and additional examinations on these sites. It happened to be the case for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 182. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is another short mission conducted in 1997, during summer 1997, or maybe April because we always started when -- as soon as April. And this -- the goal of this mission was to check if there were some human remains in the -- on this plateau of the dam, because technical means, aerial means, did not implement the theory that there was a grave there. But on the surface, for example, this is a piece of a cloth knotted looking like a ligature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 183.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same piece of cloth washed and put on concrete to take a better picture of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 184.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So during that mission that I said, the goal was to check if on the area that where we believed could be a grave was to dig. The dig was specifically difficult because it's very rocky terrain, but having dug a hole approximately 1 metre of depth, we hit the first piece of evidence which is marked by the yellow arrow. It looks like a piece of a stone or mud, but on the next picture it will be seen that it is, in fact, the top of a skull, a human skull.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 185.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same piece of evidence but washed at a water-pipe nearby. And later on this photograph was shown to our anthropologist who asserts this is a human skull.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 186.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was also during the 1997 mission, another collection of pieces of bones on the surface of the dam where the anthropologist sorts out these bits and pieces into more anthropological data pieces coming from various parts of human skulls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 187.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also part of a process we conducted on the plateau. It was to collect shell casings. And this is the result of our three hour, let's say, collection of shell casings on the plateau. There are more than 1.000 shell casings in these bags. They are all in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember the calibre or calibres of the shell casings?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 7.62 for, I think, more or less -- more or less all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And 188.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a marking that I did on the plateau that indicates the location where we found the shell casings. And, I mean, the skull fragments were in a more -- more restricted area -- the skull fragments were in a more restricted area. This is -- these are the limits where most of the shell casings were found, and this is an indication of what was the size of the terrain occupied by the dead bodies, the victims we are talking about. The aspect of the skull fragments is of relevance because there is a statement saying that at one point soldiers complained against one of the shooters that he was aiming the victims at the head, and after a while, since it was spilling their brain, they were claiming that it was stinking, so they requested him to stop this. So this is why the search for all these skull fragments was of interest also. It was an implementation of what one of the survivors overheard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go back to your video collection, take us -- we'll go back to the school, the Grbavci school. And the number for that is 1138. And, again, if need be, could you offer us any new information or narrative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you turn off the sound. I would just as soon have Mr. Ruez be the narrator. This sound is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's what I tried to explain using pictures, but now it's on videos. So this is the entrance of the school that to the right hand leads to the school building and to the left to the gym where the prisoners, as far as we know about, were kept inside. We don't know if others were kept in the classrooms. The survivors were all from the gym. So the right is the entrance towards the school building; the left towards the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall when this video was shot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did several in this location, so here I can recognise a colleague who was not with the first one, or maybe it was -- I don't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was 1996. I think it was the one of February 1996. But without the sound, I cannot say because the first one I remember because I was requesting my colleague to check if I was not hitting something dangerous, I mean, while I was filming. And this one he is filming. So this is either 1997 or 1998, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's -- at the left it's the entrance and here is the exit. This is where the people were taken out after having been blindfolded and had a sip of water. And inside you can still find these pieces of cloth that were not there the first -- the very first time, so I believe that some children were playing with abandoned material around, like, also there were a lot of shell casings and even live ammunition that I handed over to the police at the time so that the children don't play with it again. So that's summer 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is there something that makes you now recollect that it's summer?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because it's the day we went through this pile of rubbish. Here we are starting to line up the material collected in this little dump site, so shell casings. But mainly the interesting material in there is the blindfold, knowing that this school was used on a quite regular basis by the army, so the shell casings are not necessarily relevant to the events of that day, but the blindfolds, for sure they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now we have one other short. We go out -- and that is number 1155. And could you tell us, once you see this, where this is once we get going.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grbavci school again. So Orahovac area. At the top of the picture, the direction to the execution site, one can clearly see the road line on it's elevation. This is designed to show the distance between the sites, knowing that the prisoners inside the gym did not hear the shooting take place. It's partially due to the distance, but mainly because the elevation of the railroad makes a natural sound barrier. So that house did not exist at the -- in 1995. It was starting to be built in 1996. So it's behind the road line. And, again, we approach the first execution site. That's the terrain in the shape we found it when we arrived. Very muddy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So none of those ruts were done by any ICTY equipment?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. These are the traces of the initial heavy equipment used to create this site. So the man with the yellow equipment is Professor Bill Haglund, our anthropologist. And this greenish mud is due to the mixture of soil and human bodies that decomposed that created this greenish mud.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is this that they are digging around, if you recall or know?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably a piece of a bone, the top of a bone that Professor Haglund recognises as being a human bone. The sound would tell it because he probably explains. That's a piece of cloth. I don't know. That's the garbage dump site 200 metres away from the execution and burial site. That's the asphalt road that can be seen behind the bushes. The sound would be of interest because the person who is taking the video is counting the items and describing them. Socks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you tell us why there is no sound?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just thought it would be easier because it's in English and it -- if the translators can translate it, sometimes they can, then it would be okay for the General, otherwise, it's -- there is, I believe, there's a transcript of this, but I'm not sure. So let's -- why don't we try it with the sound, and if they can translate it, fine; if they can't, we can either go with the sound or without the sound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a description of items and numbers. So at least for the blindfolds, it's of interest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I am the one who is making the description. I recognise my accent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You haven't changed to a British accent now, have you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Peter Nicholson speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue on in the presentation with page 189.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just to make the situation clear. I think, Mr. Tolimir, you received B/C/S translation of the sound, the words spoken? I could hear them in B/C/S, and it was translated also in French, what we heard on the video.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Presiding Judge. I was able to hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I perhaps should offer that video into evidence. The two; one was 1138 and 1155 by our numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Both will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1138 will be Exhibit P86, and the next one will be Exhibit P87, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So now we are at page 189, and you've got a yellow marking up by the village of Rocevic. And tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's the third identified detention centre used in the so-called area north, a place called Rocevic. It is again a school that was used on 15 July and filled with another load of prisoners coming from Bratunac that was still in the process of being emptied of all the prisoners during the day of the 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 190.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a view of the school as it can be seen by zooming from the asphalt road that leads from Zvornik towards, in fact, Banja Luka, I mean, alongside of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 191.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the same school, seen from the back. So one can see that it's a larger structure with classrooms and also a gym attending [sic] to it. We do not know what part of this building has been used to store the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let's -- Mr. Ruez, you are not familiar with all the various investigations that have occurred since 2001, are you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not, that's why I was cautious about my talking about only about my personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So let's go to 192 now. And we have your map again, same yellow circle with Rocevic, and now a star near the Drina River. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the star marks the approximate placement of the execution site where these prisoners were taken to. They had to be taken towards first Kozluk and at Kozluk make a kind of U-turn in order to hit a little road going alongside the Drina valley and reach a little remote location where the execution site was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you've talked about information received from a survivor of the Luke school, the Kravica warehouse, the Orahovac and Petkovci schools, and their associated execution sites. Did you have a survivor for this site that you are talking about near Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no survivor from this execution. The information related to this site, in fact, came from an information from a person who was in a refugee centre in Germany and who was still in contact with some relatives living in the area and who were able to provide enough information in order for us to narrow down the place and finally find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to 193 where you can explain what this is and how you found it. Just briefly. Again, I don't want to put you through the entire investigation.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main thing that enabled us, the final stage, to find it was to be able to narrow it down on a map and then to request through US State Department a survey of aerial imagery in order to even more narrow down the possibilities, and that's what led us to the site. This is seen from north to south; at the left is the Drina valley. The school would be at the right-hand of the picture, but at a distance. And Kozluk town is just in front. So, in fact, one would first take the asphalt road, drive towards Kozluk, and then drive along a dirt road alongside of Drina River and hit this area of -- it was gravel pits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you were following up on this information you talked about and you first arrived at this scene that you've marked execution site, what did you find to indicate that it may have been an execution site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following pictures should show what we found when we arrived the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well there is one; 194 is the next picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. So once in Kozluk and taking this little sharp turn in order to hit the gravel road that leads towards the execution site, there are two interesting structures. The first one is a factory that embottles bottles; it's the Vitinka factory. This will be of interest because as you will see on the site there are items that connect to this factory. And later on in secondary burial sites the same items will be found and make the connection between the entire situation. So that's the first building one can hit is this Vitinka factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 195.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second structure is a military compound. It's the compound of the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 196.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's the imagery obtained by the US, from the US. So at the left you can see the Drina River. And on the picture dated 5 July, when compared with the one 17 July, it is obvious that on the 17 July there has been quite a dramatic change in the terrain in this area, with a lot of disturbed soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 197.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So seen from the ground on the area of the disturbance, one can notice that there is quite a lot of amount of broken glass, bits and pieces of broken glass, and also this part is a part of -- it's a shoe, in fact, with a bone in it - another picture will show it better - popping out of the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 198.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So again, the shoe with a stocking and a bone inside. And inside the shovel is a shell casing and a sample of this broken glass that can be found in many places in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So was this what you found when you first arrived at the scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the broken glass is in fact because these gravel pits were also used as depots for broken bottles from the Vitinka factory, and the same glass but also labels of bottles, labelled Vitinka, were later on found in secondary mass graves. In fact, the day before we went to this place, we were at a secondary site where these labels were coming out, and this is what sparked the decision to go as soon as possible to this last execution site that we had not processed yet, but it was at that point a certainty that this would be the spot. And, indeed, all the forensics done after that confirmed the fact that the two sites were linked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 199.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So here one can see a shell casing and broken glass. The little yellow sticker is just there to mark the presence of the shell casing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 200.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, again, the green broken glass and also a piece of limb that -- one piece was sticking out of the ground so we just pulled a bit on it and it appears to be human remains. So we didn't continue further excavation of this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was this site later fully exhumed by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was it found to be a disturbed or undisturbed site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an execution site on which many details are indeed provided by the reports, and this site was then disturbed and more than two-thirds of the bodies were removed from it and put in a place that we named the Cancari valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And there will be others and more detailed evidence on those matters. So let's go to your next topic; it's at page 201. And we see the yellow mark over the village of -- well I can make out Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pilica, Luke. Luke school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go to 202. And where does this fit into the story?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, again, 15 July the evacuation of Bratunac was still not fully completed. In fact, it completed that day. Among the last ones to be shipped north was a large group of prisoners who were taken to this school, the school of a location named Kula close to Pilica and close to Branjevo. So it's a quite large structure, two-storage [sic] building, and a big gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 203.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the view of -- one can see when he arrives at the school on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall any particular significance to that right side of the school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One prisoner who was inside and who the next day survived the execution at the Branjevo farm was tasked to go and fetch some water at the water-pipe, and it was night. When he was on his way back, he saw that one bus full of prisoners arrived at this location. The people were unloaded and shot on the spot at the -- just in front of this facade. So we, indeed, made also a few checks about this assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 204.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the path that the prisoners took in order to then turn right and enter the school and the gym. The gym entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 205.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the entrance; it is also the exit of the school. At the exit, this is where the people were lined and for some of them blindfolded before being taken on board of buses for alleged exchange of prisoners and, in fact, brought to the Branjevo farm for execution.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this overview shows the location of the water source where the survivor went in order to pick up water and bring back to the gym.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the water source.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did you yourself find these places after this person told you this story?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, I used the indication of the testimony that we had of him in order to find the places and match them with the description we had of it, and that's how we could find these locations --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, 2 --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- following the path he had described when he gave his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the angle of sight; the little arrow shows the angle of sight from the exit point of, way back, of the water source and the location he claimed having seen the people getting out of a bus and being shot. So, indeed, he had the possibility to have this angle of vision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we see the arrow-head on this arrow. Is that where he is or where the bus is or what?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is where -- the point of the arrow is on the gravel road, and the rest of the arrow is his line of sight of people he said had been shot were at the left of the trees, not the gravel road but at the left of the trees on the grass, having the building at their back.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And these are some traces that could still be seen on the facade and that could be connected with his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Holes on the facade of the school wall.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Holes that had been filled with concrete on the side of the wall.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Areas marked in red both on top of the picture and the picture at the bottom are the areas where we collected shell casings embedded in the ground. Which would match, indeed, the position of people who would shoot on a group close to the facade; one on the front, one on the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to 213.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, the red star is the approximate spot of the execution site of the Branjevo farm which is the location from where the -- on 16 in the morning before 10.00 the people who were inside the school of Luke were taken on board of buses and taken to the Branjevo farm, which is a military farm.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the aerial imagery of this farm, and it is dated 5th of July, so before the events. At the top of the picture, the buses were coming from the left and then entering the real estate of this farm. I will be able to give more details. It's a pigsty. So the building top right is a pigsty. The long building just in front of the top right is also a pigsty. At the bottom left is the administration building. And completely at the left is a garage. The garage was the site where the execution squad was waiting for the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why don't we, if we could, put this on e-court so that Mr. Ruez can mark this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we have an aerial marked in yellow --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Actually, the --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- with all of it on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct. So let's -- we'll just take advantage of that. Let's go to the next one, 215.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a picture taken from the ground, which gives the angle of site of someone arriving at the farm. So that's the access path we saw on the previous picture. Now the pigsty is on the left; the admin building is the one on the middle; the garage, a bit on the right; and a very large field to the right, which is the execution field. This is where the Black Hawk helicopter has landed. It's behind the helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you come in that Black Hawk?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went in by car, by helicopter; I went several times there to the Branjevo farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 216.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a helicopter view of the farm. That is a perfect indication of the size of the terrain at the right. One can perfectly see the gravel road that, from the right, is coming, in fact, from the direction of the school, then turning right towards the Branjevo farm was the area where the bus were stopped, as witnesses will say, from the windows they could see what was happening because it was not happening at a very long distance since the people had to walk towards the garage, which is the little structure to the right, extreme right of the picture, right of the farm. And then they started to shoot them from there. And then the people had to continue to walk over the bodies until they could find the tree line. And this was continuing like this towards the right side of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I think it would be helpful if we could put this one on e-court. And if you could just mark this area where the survivors told you the executions were going on.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the buses were coming like this. Then they were parking here. Sometimes there were several. People then had to walk like this. Here was the location where the execution squad was having his, in brackets, "rest place." And then the people had to line up in rows. It was -- the process was continuing like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I would offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, that will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P88, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we can go to 217 now.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the view one has when arriving at the garage I was just describing. And so that's the starting point of the execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 218.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the -- that's the execution field as it was the first time we approached it. And we did a quick check on the site. It was the first approach; I think it was in March 1996. And it was two hours on the spot and only with a drawing of an aerial imagery that was of assistance to find the place, so it took a little while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, can you tell from being there, was this churned up soil, did this appear to be from agricultural or from the kind of churned up soil you had seen at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say because it's agricultural ground. It had been moved upside-down when we really came to process the area. But, indeed, yes, we know that the place had been also turned upside-down at the time on 17 July where the bodies were cleaned off the ground to be buried in a mass grave just very close by of this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So -- but was there a cornfield planted there at around the times that you visited after, you know, after this incident, at various times?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it stayed more or less after that abandoned terrain. And now it's a settlement of housing. This place does not exist any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 26.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So among the items we could see the first time we arrived was, for example, a -- one shoe in the bushes.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Human bones, a piece of hip and a rib and another bone.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a human skull.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture dated 17 July, the interest of it -- well, there are two interests. One is that we don't show it, maybe you will have to, is the US markings that are on a similar picture with a closer shot, that indicates that many of the dots seen on the picture are labelled by the US as being bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say dots, where are the dots that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the same one that I saw on the right screen. Yeah, now it's this one. In between the two lines, the two yellow lines on the right. But the two yellow lines are there to show that when we came there in order to do a shell casing collection on the surface, that might have been in 1997, indeed the field had already been plundered. So the number of shell casings on the surface we found was relatively limited. I cannot remember exactly how many. But what was interesting was the repartition of them on the ground since, in fact, we started to find them very shortly after the garage, so matching the beginning of the execution field and all along -- all along this field on quite a long distance close to 200 metres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think when you said the field when you got there had already been plundered, you may have meant ploughed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ploughed, sorry, yeah, yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And this area where we see some sorts of dots or something between the yellow lines, is this anywhere near the area that you just marked on the map where the people told you the executions happened?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's both the location where the people said the execution happened, but also it's the location where we found the items seen on the previous pictures; the shoes, the skull, the bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And aside from the survivor evidence that you are talking about, did you have any shooter evidence; anybody that took part in the shooting that corroborated that same information?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. All this is also part of the testimony of Drazden Erdemovic. Most of it is part of the testimony of Erdemovic. The fact that the garage was the rest place for the execution squad of a 10 Sabotage Detachment and their colleagues from the Bratunac Brigade is coming from Drazden Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And that will be a witness you will hear from, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could go to 223. I think this is what you referred -- reminded me of.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no, because in yellow are my markings, but the fact is that my markings on this one reproduce the US markings. So maybe taking the original US into evidence would be something to be done later. But when I write on the yellow -- orange line "bodies," the line with the "bodies," this is what was written on the US imagery. Also, the label "piles of earth" is on the original US imagery. The label "probable bodies" put in a pile close to the location where an excavator is digging and where we found the location of the primary mass grave, all this were markings on the initial US imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But just to reiterate, you are not certainly relying totally on the US imagery for this information, but other parts of the investigation and fieldwork?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The goal is also to check on the ground the assertions put on official pictures. And as you will see on another picture, the location where the excavator is digging, so most probably creating a grave, there were even also surface remains at that location. And then for sure subsequently the exhumation, full exhumation, conducted on this spot fully confirms what can be seen on this aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And that will be the subject of other witnesses, other reports. All right. Let's go now to 224. We have imagery dated 21 September and 5 July. What's the purpose of this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the purpose of this one is, if you check the ground at the beginning of the yellow arrow starting with the picture right-hand 5th July, terrain is undisturbed; and if you compare it with the one of 21 September, there is a clear disturbance. And this is the spot where we started to check both for surface evidence and then sparked an exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was that -- was there a grave found to be there where that yellow arrow-head is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was it determined to be disturbed or undisturbed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following pictures will show it more clearly, but, yes, it was disturbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 225.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a picture taken just at the edge of the area of disturbed soil. It's human remains. One can see it's part of the bottom of a spine on the picture. That had been pushed just in the bushes by the excavator who buried the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We now have your videos of first Kozluk and then Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there are a few, two or three, I think, following this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We get to -- we'll get to the Pilica Dom right after this.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Kozluk is 1195. And we'll start with that short clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I guess we can have sound, if there is any. And thank you for trying to interpret. We appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a video of the first arrival at the Kozluk site. So broken glass. Human remains, bones. In fact, it's a leg with some cloth around it. The shoe with the sock and a bone in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's no sound on this, so thank you for narrating.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's another shoe, I think. It's fuzzy. A big pile of broken glass. This is investigator Jan Kryszewski looking for shell casings alongside of the dirt road that is just next to the area where the human remains are popping out of the soil, so it's a shell casing found. Another shell casing. Shell casing again. That's the shovel we saw, a better quality picture we see it on video. That's a very short excavation we started. And we realised that in fact it was a very, very shallow grave. And just by pulling out some elements, in fact, we are beginning an exhumation, so the place was worth being fully exhumed. Approximate number of people killed on this spot is around 500. And the location is on the spot of a former Muslim cemetery that has been destroyed. These are labels from the embottlement factory. We found exactly the same labels in three secondary mass graves. This is why we can know the precise number of people killed there by adding those who were found in the primary grave and adding the numbers of those found in the secondary ones. That's why the total number reaches close to 500.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, at your time, you didn't -- all the graves had not been exhumed yet, so would you be open for the possibility of those numbers changing?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, though the three secondary graves for Kozluk, we already know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where is -- we've now switched from the grave to some place else. Where is this still now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is when we are driving back and passing by the Drina Wolves barracks, if I'm not wrong. Yes. I got out of the car and was filming the passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, do you associate the Drina Wolves in any way with any of these executions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, because I can't. I can only observe that their barracks are extremely close by, but we have no -- as far as I know, no admittance, no hard evidence, and nothing that connects them to the killing on that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That remains the case today.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the embottlement factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What you have referred to as the Vitinka bottle factory?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's the patch of the Drina Wolves. That's the exhumation -- the beginning of the exhumation at Kozluk, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And done by who?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Richard Haglund was the head archaeologist on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Richard ...

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Richard Wright.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I believe we have a video of Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I'd offer that last one into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That was 1195, our number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P89, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now we have our number 1232 of Branjevo and related material.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember when you were flying over Branjevo, what year that was?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I flew twice, but this was probably again in the preparation of the trial of General Krstic, so in 1998, I would think. So, yeah, okay. This was -- the goal of this one is to show the distance between the Branjevo farm and the village of Pilica, that is along the asphalt road going on this natural road from Zvornik towards Banja Luka and Janja and going north toward Banja Luka. Now, in fact, this one is first from the school to the farm, so that's the way from the school to the farm. That's the farm. That's the large field. Here at the angle is the mass grave. That's the structure. So the farm abandoned at that time. The grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I've just frozen it there. Can you orient us to what you've previously described? You can't mark on this, unfortunately, with a video, but I think that there's some things that we hopefully will remember.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we -- one can see the garage at the right of the picture, the white rectangle, that is the garage. So at the top of it is the tree, and then if you take a straight line to the left, there is -- one can see a separation. So from the tree to the left it's the area of the execution field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And there's something growing there now. Do you remember what?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember something was growing, but I don't know what it was. I'm not a botanist, I repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, let's just continue then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably corn. So that's the access path to the farm with, again, at the right, the two pigsties, at the bottom left the admin building, and above the admin building one can see the garage. Again here there is a lot of things growing on the area, which again shows that time runs against evidence. Had we had to mow this huge field in order to find a few shell casings, it would still be in process.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did the buses bringing the prisoners park?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just along this access path. Sometimes there were a few buses jamming there, so the passengers in -- I mean, the witnesses will better talk about this than I would do, but it would see everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's the bottom. One could see the asphalt road going to -- from Zvornik north to Janja. So that was the second -- one was in March but very, very short, and this one was in April 1996. Peter Nicholson is talking and filming. These are press people. That's the area where the mass grave was supposed to be and where we made the first and the second quick observations on the ground. That's the body parts that was at the edge of this grave. Third mission to the farm. Oh, it was more than third. So that is the execution area. That's where the people were arriving. And starting at the tree, execution field began. That's the day we were looking for the shell casings on the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What are these things?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shell casings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Is that the field that's now full of houses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The place would be unrecognisable. We were looking for a bridge one of the survivors talked about. It's a bridge after he crawled away from the crime scene. He hid under a bridge where there were destroyed vehicles. So we were looking around also to try to identify a location that could match his declarations, and this is indeed the location he was hiding under, at least that perfectly matched his description.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Any destroyed vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several. And we brought him back, anyhow, to that site, and he recognised the locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't see Humvees anymore. Can you tell us what troops are providing the security for you now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Russian troops were securing our missions at the north of this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who were driving the Humvees that we saw in the Konjevic Polje area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: American forces. It's -- the multi-national division north had control on the area that includes the crime scene, south being on the American sector, and north being the Russian sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Okay, let's go to the next chapter. It's 226.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we'll offer that clip into evidence. It's 1232, our number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P90, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this time we see --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branjevo we already dealt with. Next one will be Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So let's go to 227. What does this have to do with the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So following the events at the Branjevo farm that took place from 10.00 in the morning through approximately 3.00 in the afternoon, the order was given to the executioners of that place to move towards a location nearby where allegedly 500 people were stored into a Dom of culture, a cultural house, and had to be killed. So the squads moved towards this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you get that information?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information is coming purely from the Drazen Erdemovic. We have no survivor of that spot. Without his declarations on this crime scene, we would never had received any info about this location and the events that took place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so did you go there and check this out?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so what is this picture we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So on this picture, since according his declaration, the group he was with, the 10 Sabotage Detachment guys did not take place in these specific killings; they were in a cafe just in front of the Dom of culture. So, indeed, there is a cafe just in front, and the next arrow shows the location of the Dom of culture. He was witnessing the events from the cafe across the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to 228.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's a front view of this house of culture. So, in fact, this is the admin building; it's kind of a little town hall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you shortly. The Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes, could you just go back to the previous picture. Yes. I have a question for the witness. In this picture, you are showing the Dom Kulture as a place of execution; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: And what are those other houses around this place in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took care selecting, going from south to north, locations which are at a distance of housings. But since all the available facilities, the Grbavci school, the Rocevic School, the Luke school, all these places were full, the last prisoners that had to be taken north were taken to this place which is at 100 metres away from the border between the Drina Corps and the corps which was just north. And they never did anything in the area of responsibility of anyone else. So the last location was this one. And all around, indeed, you are in the middle of a village. So the Grbavci school, there are also a few houses around. It's a very tiny village. This one is a bigger village. So all these places were, indeed -- there were citizens there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: At the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this road we're looking at, how significant is this road as a route from north to south or south to north?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the only main route that leads from north to south of the Republika Srpska along the Drina Valley. It's the main road going north to south.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's, okay then, go back to 228. I think you may have been almost done. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the view from the front. Seen from the road, this is the view of this Dom of culture. At the time, because it's totally changed also since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to one more picture before the break, it's 229.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a view of the cafe where the guys from the 10 Sabotage Detachment were looking at the events, meanwhile having drinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. This may be a good time to take a break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have a break now for 30 minutes and resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We were at -- we had a picture of the cafe across the street from the cultural centre. Now, let's go to 230, your next series of shots. There's the -- that was 229. Let's -- now we are at 230. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken from the inside of a cafe towards the house of culture of Pilica. So one can see that there is, in fact, a little metal structure, little construction, that hides the view, the direct view, on the exit of the area that was used as the execution spot. But as the witness said, he could still see things that he will probably talk about, people managing to get out and being shot in the street, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Indeed. Okay. Let's go to 231.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a side view when approaching this Dom of culture. The theatre part of it is on the right side of this building. The entrance door being the blue one at the right of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 232.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two access to the place. The metal door at the right is the entrance to this theatre area. The blue door, wooden, at the left gets to a staircase that accesses to the cabin of projector, the person who was playing films, if this, in bracket, "theatre" was used as a movie place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 233.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture is to show that when we arrived to this spot the door had been closed with a "cadenas." And obviously this "cadenas" had not been removed since the cleanup of the place since there are spider nests in between the two openings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall when you first got there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in 1996, end of 1996. I would think August maybe. Mid -- I don't remember when.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We opened this "cadenas."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's with the padlock, in English. I think you are talking about the lock?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, padlock. The lock, yes. Padlock.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 234. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of an inside of a theatre seen from the location where there are little openings that enable the camera to project the film, and this was the -- most certainly the first area where the shooting started, since after the shooting had started from this location, only then did soldiers enter through the main door and continue the killing inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 235.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So indeed it's August 1996, so this is a sample collection, the first sample collection that we did on the walls of the -- inside the theatre.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an example of the type of the stains that were on the walls. In this specific case, it's human blood and hair and pieces of skin.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same type of picture, blood-stain and bullet-holes.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the back of the theatre when climbing on the stage, a very characteristic blood-stain in that location.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the wall totally at the back of the stage, since the killers shooting from the top and also those entering the main door. The people apparently took refuge in this last shelter area where grenades were thrown, even underneath the wooden structure, because people were probably hiding underneath, so these are traces that have been analysed as being explosive traces and also blood traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say explosive traces, what colour are we looking at of those traces in this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The black ones are explosive residues and the stains are blood-stains.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 240. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an aerial imagery where indeed originally my markings in yellow where the truck was marked but the traces of the rear door; I marked the rear door. The 17 July is the day that followed this execution and is the day of cleanup of this execution site. At the location of the truck which is right at the main entrance of the building, we didn't collect them but there were a few remains, like rubber gloves. That's the cleanup. One survivor, who -- the one who was hiding under the bridge, also that day get out of this location and was along the asphalt road and he saw a truck going direction south which is the direction of Branjevo farm with a body full of remains with even some blood spilling out of it. So that was probably a truck coming from the location of Pilica. The bodies of those killed in Pilica have been transported for burial, the 17 at the Branjevo farm. So the burial at the Branjevo farm is both the burial of the victims killed at the Branjevo farm and at the Pilica Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you mark in yellow, you say "traces;" what are you pointing at there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since these traces are going also to the back of the building, one can assume that the cleaning of the place was done by both sides, the main entrance and also the rear door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So, in your view, what were those traces made by?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: By a truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 241. What does this tell us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows the direction that goes from the Dom towards the Branjevo farm, which is very close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now you've -- we have another video of about 10 minutes of this Dom of culture which we will play.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is our first arrival at the ... The office of the mayor was at the first floor, and there was also a civilian communication centre inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So is this your very first arrival?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the very first one, because initially, according to the first statement we had, but we didn't took by ourselves, of Drazen Erdemovic, we were first looking for this location but in Janja, so some 40 or 50 kilometres more north. That was the cafe just across the road. The inside. One wall had been sealed after the events. There was an access to the theatre that has been blocked. But someone did an opening top-right so one can peep into it. That's the little communication centre. That's the sealed door, fresh concrete. That's what one could see peering through this little hole. And just in the vicinity, indeed housings. That's from the openings of the projectionist cabin. Though the place had been cleaned, there were still a number of shell casings on the stairs going up to this location, this cabin. The main door at the bottom right. That's the projectionist cabin, and this is the stairs going down. Here in the corner, the broomer forgot a shell casing. Some more shell casings on the stairs. That's the environment of the place. The Russian escort. The cafe. A rubber glove just in front of the entrance. Now we open the door. That's the holes from the projectionist cabin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So is this still that first time when you -- this is the first time you walked in there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the very first time, yeah. I was on the left, John Gerns is in front, and Peter Nicholson is filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember what month this was, what year?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at the beginning of the tape it was August 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How many people did Mr. Erdemovic estimate were in here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were told by the lieutenant-colonel who ordered them to go to this location, he said that there were 500 prisoners inside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you stop at that point for a moment. A question from Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just a question, Witness. The film we've just seen, this is when you arrived in August 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. I even returned for, in bracket, "private means" in that location in, it was, I think, in 2003, and the place was in exactly in the same shape. Any forensic expert could have returned there and collect hundreds of samples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The question of Judge Mindua was not interpreted. Mr. Tolimir, did you receive interpretation of this question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Presiding Judge. The question was interpreted to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another question by Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Actually, it's a follow-up question to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am advised that it needs to be repeated because the question is not on the transcript because it was not translated into English. We were all on the French channel for that moment. Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall repeat my question. The witness said that he arrived at Pilica in August 1996 for the first time. And my question was, therefore, to know whether at that time on the walls of the Kulture Dom it was possible to see blood-stains, pieces of skin, hair, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. My answer to that was that, yes, absolutely. As I had exposed also this place had been sealed off after the cleanup process of it, so then it was untouched. Proof of it is the locker and the spider nests in between the doors. And, in addition to that, these places have been untouched for years, and I did happen to return there, I think, in 2003, it might have been 2002, but the same -- exactly the same things were inside. And they said any forensic expert who had gone there even in 2002 or 2003 would have collected hundreds of blood-stains. The situation is the same in the Kravica warehouse. The place has never been fully cleaned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we have the situation clear on the record. Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes. If you go back to page 35, line 16, you state there that this is our first arrival at ... "The office of the mayor was at the first floor." Was the office of the mayor on the first floor of this building in which the executions took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we were told upon arrival when we were asking, you know, what is this place. First thing was, Oh, it's the office of the mayor upstairs, and here it's telecommunication, civilian telecommunication centre. And do you know if anything happened there? For sure the answer was, We don't understand why you are here; nothing ever happened here. And one hour later, everyone had vanished before we opened the door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. McCloskey, with the film.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are a few items we did find during this first check. This was the cover of a licna karta, I think. Brown. The shell casing. I mean, the shell casings were mainly to be found in the corners due to the brooming of the place, but it was done very roughly. Some ID pieces with one with a legible name on it. That person appeared on the missing list of the ICRC as missing from Srebrenica. This one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to your next chapter. It starts at page 242.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But let me offer that into evidence. It's our number 1256.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P91, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just -- we see this diagram, crime scenes area north, and you've marked the places that we've just talked about. What's the purpose of this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is, in fact, a summary of the main spots of the so-called area north, so in yellow the places that had been selected for the detention of the prisoners, and the red stars spotting the execution sites of these prisoners. Knowing that this is not extremely accurate, it's a graphic to indicate the main locations and how they fit together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 243.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same type of map. It's the situation at 17 July, so the day where the exhumation process is finalised. Executions being finished the 16, burial totally finished the 17. So on 17 July 1995, this is the status of the known situation regarding mass graves. Those we went through, area north and also area south with one that we had not discussed yet, which is the main one in the area south, that is, Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 244. Now we are getting into a series of these aerial imagery. And what's the purposes of this section?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as the exhumation process made us realise at the end of summer 1996, in the main places that we could exhume during that summer, we realised that indeed it was a massive burial places, but that these mass graves had been emptied of part of their content and we didn't know how much of their content. Was it half? Was it 80 per cent? We had no idea. So checking the situation with aerial imagery, we could sort out that indeed these places had been subject to a further disturbance. So this is Orahovac, the execution site close to Grbavci school. On the picture at the left, one can see the scale of the disturbance dated the 7 September, so after the primary burial. And then one can see that on 27 September the situation is clearly very different. So this place has again been turned upside-down and looks differently now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That's one of the sites that you spoke of at the Orahovac. Let's go to 245. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, again, it's exactly the same. This is the site LZ-1 where, on 7 September, we can see the shape of the disturbance. And on 27 September 1995, less than one month later, the disturbance has completely changed. So it has been redisturbed again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are these disturbances the detailed subject of the forensic archaeologist and anthropology reports that go along with this investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. Everything about it is in the reports of the specialists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So, again, you're not relying on these -- purely these aerial imageries for these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. It's complementary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 246. We are now back to the Petkovci dam, I see.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the disturbance, anyhow, was so small that it could not be spotted before checking the disturbance. This is why the primary assumption was that there was no mass grave on this plateau because aerial imagery could not show obvious disturbance. But knowing that indeed there was a mass grave there because we found the elements, then by comparing the photograph dated 7 September with then and obvious disturbance 27 September, we could also figure out that this location had also been disturbed, which was then later on confirmed once the full exhumation of this area took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 247, we go on to Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, again, exactly the same situation. The shape of the terrain, 7 September, after the burial of the victims had taken place there, and on the 27 September, a much larger disturbance indicating that additional work had been done between the 7 September and end of September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 248.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one is even more clear because this is an aerial from Branjevo farm dated 27 September where these markings are US markings. One can see, exactly at the location where the mass grave was located, a newly excavated trench that did not exist after the burial process, so after the 17 of July. And imagery analysts would say that indeed inside the farm there is still a backhoe and a front loader. By looking at the original picture, indeed one can see them.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a picture that was taken at the end of the exhumation of Branjevo farm, so at the end of the summer 1996. This is the full size of the initial mass grave site. And where the three persons are standing, it's the only spot inside this grave where bodies could be found. All the rest had been taken out of this large hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we go back to the last photograph, 248. Is this that hole that we just saw anywhere near --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This hole is at the location where it is now written "newly excavated trench."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 250.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture is the picture of the bodies that were found during the exhumation of the Branjevo farm. So the only bodies left in the larger hole we saw previously is this stack of body. I think the total number in the exhumation report is something like 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you mentioned the one grave that we hadn't spent a chapter on was Glogova. We're coming to some pictures. Could you just again, very briefly, tell us the story where Glogova is and how it fit into the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Glogova is in a location in between Kravica and Bratunac, going from Kravica towards Bratunac. And Glogova ended up to be -- I mean, after having started the cleaning process of Kravica warehouse, the first bodies were taken to a remote location not far away from the asphalt road on a -- and dumped alongside of a slope on a hill and covered with soil. But they only did that with a few trucks. Later, the decision was made to open a disposal place at Glogova. And Glogova became the spot where they dumped all the bodies of those killed at the Kravica warehouse. But unfortunately not only that - and this is why we will never have a hundred per cent certainty of the number of killed at Kravica by counting these bodies - the fact is that Glogova was also used to bury in graves all the bodies killed in Bratunac town, and there were a certain number of them, but also the place where they did put the bodies of people killed alongside of the asphalt road. So the burial site of Glogova, the bodies have multiple origins. It's a mixture of several origins that make it impossible to determine from where these people are coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you mention some bodies along the asphalt road. Can you exclude the possibility that some of those people were killed in combat trying to cross the road?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one can ever exclude someone willing to commit suicide, but as soon as someone reaches the asphalt road, he is there to surrender, as a logical point. So if he gets killed there, it means that something has happened. But I have no explanation about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So let's go to our first photograph of Glogova. It's 251. And this is dated well after the events of Kravica of 13 July. It's dated October. What's the purpose of this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this one is this is a shot that indeed indicates even the date during which this disturbance of Glogova takes place, since Glogova is split in two areas of graves. It's not one mass grave; it's several graves at the right and a few others at the left. And on 30 October, there is a front loader busy exhuming one part of the Glogova graves. It can be seen on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go now to 252. What is this illustration?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a visual of the sites area south, the red arrows are the mass graves that have not been disturbed. At the right of Kravica, the little red star is the site along this edge of the little hill that has not been disturbed. But the two main sites of this area which are at Glogova have been wiped out of most of their content. And the bodies, the yellow arrow shows the direction, in fact, they were transported at the opposite side of the Srebrenica safe area, completely south of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 253.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
